title: Rav Idi, Attendant of Rav Sheshet
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Bekhorot 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.31b.9): he stated a teaching of Rav Sheshet without attributing it to him. Rav Sheshet took offense and said, “Whoever stung me—let a scorpion sting him.”[^1][^2]

notes.text: סרסיה means ‘his attendant,’ as [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Bekhorot.31b.9) explains (שמעיה). Rashi understands the scorpion’s sting as excommunication.
The Wikisource heading has Rav Idi; the cited Bekhorot passage has Rabbi Idi.
